review_candidates.description: HR Business Partner – Employee Relations & HR Operations About the Role Our client is looking for an HR Business Partner with deep expertise in Employee Relations (ER) and HR Operations to support one or more of its client accounts. This is an individual-contributor, SME-level role – you will not manage a team, but you will be the go-to HR expert for the accounts you support, owning ER cases and HR Ops end-to-end. Responsibilities • Serve as the primary point of contact for employee relations matters – investigations, grievances, performance concerns, disciplinary processes, and conflict resolution – ensuring fair, consistent, and legally sound handling. • Own end-to-end HR Operations for supported client accounts, including onboarding/offboarding, documentation, HRIS data integrity, policy administration, compliance tracking, and reporting. • Advise people managers and employees on HR policies, procedures, and best practices. • Partner closely with Spoke’s clients to understand their culture and business needs, adapting HR practices to fit fast-paced, evolving environments. • Proactively identify and help resolve HR risks, escalating complex ER cases where needed. • Maintain compliance with local labor law and internal policy while supporting a startup-style, non-traditional HR culture. • Collaborate cross-functionally and flex support across time zones, coordinating with US-based stakeholders when required. Qualifications • Strong, demonstrated expertise in Employee Relations and HR Operations (SME-level, not a general HR generalist). • Background in EOR (Employer of Record) or BPO/outsourced HR environments. • Must NOT be coming from large, traditional BPO players – we’re looking for candidates with startup agility and adaptability, not enterprise-process rigidity. • Experience with smaller, non-traditional organizations that challenge or disrupt outdated HR practices is a strong plus – these candidates are encouraged to apply and will be prioritized for interviews. • Demonstrated flexibility and comfort operating in a startup/scale-up environment – ambiguity, fast change, and lean processes are the norm, not the exception. • Comfortable working independently as an individual contributor / SME, with no direct reports. • Strong communication, judgment, and case-handling skills. • Willing and able to work onsite daily in Makati, with flexibility to extend hours to cover US time zones as needed.

review_candidates.description: Human Resources London, Manchester Fully Remote Global Talent Acquisition Scheduling Coordinator Great Team, Opportunity for Career & Professional Development, Collaborative and Meritocratic work culture and Supportive Leadership About Us At Medius, we believe managing finance should be about strategy, not stress. That same mindset shapes not only the solutions we build, but also the culture we create for our people. We remove complexity, embrace innovation, and give our teams the freedom to focus on what truly matters — whether that’s transforming the future of finance with AI or finding balance to go home on time. Founded in Sweden in 2001, Medius has grown from a local startup into a global leader in cloud-based spend management solutions. Today, thousands of organizations worldwide trust us to simplify accounts payable and spend management processes. Our journey has been driven by continuous innovation, a passion for technology, and above all — the people who make it happen. We’re more than a software company. We’re a team of problem-solvers, innovators and collaborators working together to reinvent the category of accounts payable. Our solutions use Artificial Intelligence to eliminate manual work, bring clarity, confidence, and control, and empower finance teams of the future. At Medius, our values guide how we work and grow together: Connect – We believe in the power of people—individually and collectively—and our success depends on understanding and respecting each other. We appreciate that ‘empowering finance teams of the future’ is an exciting endeavor, and we share it with everyone around us. Question – We enjoy the challenge of our work and the thrill of collaboration. We are not afraid to question ourselves and each other because we believe diverse perspectives can lead to better outcomes and that there is great power in resolution. Own – We are thorough, thoughtful, and decisive. We anticipate what’s next, what a customer might need, and then we deliver. That’s how we get things done. And that’s how we remain a leader. Customers trust us to do our job so that they can focus on what they do best. At Medius, you’ll join a diverse, global community where curiosity is celebrated, ideas matter, and innovation never stops. If you’re passionate about technology, eager to make an impact, and ready to grow alongside a team that lives its values, Medius is where you can do your best work — your impact is global. Learn more at www.medius.com Job Overview Great interviews start with good timing. You'll line up candidates, interviewers and rooms so everyone shows up ready and nobody's left wondering. Candidates feel looked after. Recruiters and hiring managers get their time back for the work that matters. Responsibilities And Duties Book interviews. From phone screens to final panels, across time zones and busy calendars. Be the friendly face for candidates. Send confirmations and reminders, share logistics, and answer questions fast. Keep things tidy. Make sure our applicant tracking system and calendars match, every time. Work with recruiters and hiring managers. Suggest templates, checklists and small process fixes that save everyone a few clicks. Handle candidate details with care. Follow our data privacy practices, always. Reporting to the Country Head of Indonesia, the successful candidate will initially spend approximately 12 to 24 months with the Indonesia investment team, gaining exposure to portfolio analysis, shareholder engagement, strategic projects, financial analysis, evaluation of new investment opportunities, and market-related work. As part of a lean and growing team, the Corporate Finance Manager will closely collaborate with colleagues in Indonesia, Singapore a[PP1.1]nd Hong Kong, as well as senior stakeholders across Jardine Matheson’s portfolio businesses. This exposure will build a strong understanding of the company’s culture, operating model and approach to financial management, governance and shareholder engagement. The position is designed as a long-term development opportunity. Subject to business needs, individual performance and readiness, the successful candidate may progress into a broader finance or related leadership role within one of Jardine Matheson’s portfolio businesses. Portfolio and Financial Analysis •      Monitor and analyse the financial and operational performance of portfolio businesses, including performance against budgets, business plans and strategic priorities. •      Prepare financial analysis, management papers, business reviews and presentations to support senior management and shareholder decision-making. •      Identify and communicate material financial trends, business risks, performance gaps and value-creation opportunities. •      Support financial planning, forecasting, valuation and scenario analysis across relevant businesses and strategic initiatives. •      Develop a strong understanding of the key commercial and operational drivers affecting Jardine Matheson’s businesses in Indonesia. Investment and Business Opportunities •      Conduct in-depth commercial, strategic and financial analysis of potential investment opportunities, including market assessment, financial modelling, valuation, investment returns and business-case development. •      Assess industry dynamics, market attractiveness, business fundamentals and key investment risks to support informed investment decision-making. •      Support due diligence, transaction evaluation and execution-related activities, working with internal stakeholders and external advisers as required. •      Monitor market, industry, competitive and macroeconomic developments in Indonesia to identify emerging trends, investment themes, risks and potential opportunities relevant to Jardine Matheson’s activities. Shareholder Engagement and Strategic Support •      Support regular engagement with portfolio company management and finance teams to understand business performance, priorities and key issues. •      Assist the Country Head of Indonesia and investment team in preparing for shareholder discussions, management reviews and strategic meetings. •      Coordinate relevant initiatives across the Indonesia office, Hong Kong and portfolio companies, ensuring clear alignment and follow-through. •      Contribute to strategic reviews, market studies and special projects through structured analysis and practical execution support. •      Build effective working relationships with senior finance and business stakeholders across Jardine Matheson and its portfolio companies.
